ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are two food chains in the figure. A is labeled “Great Plains food chain for Native Americans”, in which the boxes are sequentially “Perennial grass” to “Buffalo” to “Humans”, with arrows pointing from perennial grass to buffalo, and then from buffalo to humans. B is labeled “Great Plains food chain for Europeans”, in which “Annual Crop” has an arrow pointing to “Humans”. Reasoning: In a food chain or food web, arrows indicate that energy is transferred from the food source being eaten to the consumer. Perennial grass is located at the starting point of the chain and transfers energy to buffalo, this consumer, so the role of perennial grass is to provide energy for consumers.
